rules.title: Keyboard focus is not visible
rules.expected: When you press Tab, the control that receives focus shows a clear outline or highlight.
rules.whyItMatters: People who get around with a keyboard instead of a mouse need to see where they are on the page. Without a visible mark they cannot tell which button or link the next key press will use.
rules.fixHint: Give this control a `:focus-visible` style such as a 2px outline, and remove any `outline: none` that has no replacement.

rules.title: The focus indicator is too faint
rules.expected: The focus mark is easy to tell apart from what is behind it, with a contrast ratio of at least 3 to 1.
rules.whyItMatters: A focus mark that blends into the background is nearly as bad as none. People with low vision, or anyone looking at a screen in bright light, cannot find it.
rules.fixHint: Change the colour of this control's focus outline so it has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against the background next to it.

rules.title: No hover feedback on a clickable control
rules.expected: A button or link looks different when the pointer is over it, for example a new background colour, an underline or a shadow.
rules.whyItMatters: Hover feedback tells people a control can be clicked before they click it. Without it the page feels dead and people hesitate.
rules.fixHint: Add a `:hover` style to this control that changes its background colour, text colour or underline.

rules.title: Text is unreadable against its background
rules.expected: Text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 against its background, or 3 to 1 when the text is large.
rules.whyItMatters: Text this faint is hard to read for almost everyone, impossible for people with low vision, and gone on a phone in sunlight. Whatever it says is lost.
rules.fixHint: Darken the text colour or lighten its background until the contrast ratio is at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text).

rules.title: Text contrast is below the minimum
rules.expected: Text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 against its background, or 3 to 1 when the text is large.
rules.whyItMatters: Text just under the minimum is readable on a good screen but tiring for many people, and hard to read with low vision or in bright light.
rules.fixHint: Darken the text colour or lighten its background until the contrast ratio is at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text).

rules.title: Tap target is smaller than 24 by 24 pixels
rules.expected: Every button, link and field is at least 24 by 24 pixels, or has enough empty space around it to be tapped without hitting a neighbour.
rules.whyItMatters: Small targets are hard to hit with a finger, a trackpad or an unsteady hand. People tap the wrong thing, or give up.
rules.fixHint: Make this control at least 24 by 24 pixels, for example with padding or `min-width` and `min-height`, or leave at least 24 pixels of space around it.

rules.title: Control cannot be reached with the keyboard
rules.expected: Everything you can click can also be reached with the Tab key and used with Enter or Space.
rules.whyItMatters: People who cannot use a mouse, including many screen reader and switch users, are shut out of anything the keyboard cannot reach. If it is a main action, they cannot use the app.
rules.fixHint: Make this control a real `<button>` or `<a href>` element, or at least give it `tabindex=0` and key handlers for Enter and Space.

rules.title: A positive tabindex forces a custom focus order
rules.expected: Tab moves through the page in the order things appear on screen, with no tabindex above 0 forcing a different order.
rules.whyItMatters: A positive tabindex pulls its control to the front of the Tab order, so the keyboard jumps around the page in a way nobody can predict.
rules.fixHint: Remove the positive `tabindex` from this element, and if the Tab order is wrong, reorder the elements in the HTML instead.

rules.title: Keyboard focus lands on something that cannot be seen
rules.expected: Every control that Tab lands on can be seen on screen, and is not invisible, off screen or covered by something else.
rules.whyItMatters: The person pressing Tab sees nothing happen, so they do not know where they are, and pressing Enter may trigger something they cannot see.
rules.fixHint: Make this element visible when it receives focus, or take it out of the Tab order if it is not meant to be used.

rules.title: Keyboard focus gets stuck
rules.expected: Tab always moves focus on and Shift+Tab always moves it back, so no one gets stuck on a single control.
rules.whyItMatters: Someone using only a keyboard who gets stuck cannot leave the control or reach anything else on the page. Their only way out is to reload or give up.
rules.fixHint: Remove the code that keeps this element focused, such as a key handler that blocks Tab or a blur handler that calls `focus()`, unless it is an open dialog that closes on Escape.

rules.title: The page scrolls sideways at this screen size
rules.expected: The page fits the width of the screen, so you never have to scroll sideways to read it, apart from things like wide tables that scroll inside their own box.
rules.whyItMatters: On a phone, a page that scrolls sideways hides content off screen and is awkward to read and use. It is one of the most visible signs that a site was not checked on a small screen.
rules.fixHint: Make the elements reported as overflowing fit the screen width, for example with `max-width: 100%`, wrapping text, or `overflow-x: auto` on their own container instead of the page.

rules.title: Text is cut off without an ellipsis
rules.expected: Text that does not fit its box wraps onto more lines or ends with an ellipsis, so it never just stops.
rules.whyItMatters: Text cut off mid-word hides part of the message, and the reader cannot tell that something is missing. They may act on a half-read label.
rules.fixHint: Let the text wrap, give its container more room, or add `text-overflow: ellipsis` so the cut-off is visible.
